summary: HR AC-05 sensitive-read purpose/legal-basis policy foundation with pure domain validation and metadata-only sensitive-read audit app envelope.

findings: The domain function does one thing: validate purpose-bound sensitive HR read metadata and return a classified decision.
The app function only projects a validated decision into an audit envelope and performs no authorization middleware, data retrieval, storage, network I/O, or audit-chain emission.
The slice establishes a policy/audit seam suitable for later centralized authorization and audit adapters without coupling HR domain code to runtime infrastructure.
Purpose, legal basis, policy ref, basis/request/read-log evidence, and consent evidence are explicit, deterministic fields.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if sensitive HR reads can be allowed without purpose binding, legal basis, consent evidence for consent basis, safe read logging evidence, or the sensitive-read policy prefix.
findings: AC-05 now has direct positive/negative domain coverage plus app-envelope handoff coverage.
Types mirror the acceptance wording: SensitiveHrDataKind, SensitiveReadPurpose, SensitiveReadLegalBasis, SensitiveHrReadInput, and SensitiveHrReadDecision.
Test names match the HR AC-05 spec ref and demonstrate required purpose/legal-basis/evidence fields.
cargo fmt, focused HR domain/app tests, focused HR domain/app clippy, and 12-package enterprise regression tests/clippy passed locally.
No dependencies, catalog rows, lockfile changes, runtime adapters, storage, or transport contracts were added in this slice.

The app envelope carries a stable sensitive-read audit topic plus policy, basis, consent, request, and read-log evidence refs for future adapters.
